absent: Core kill and reap implementations behind the referenced kill and reap helpers.
Reaper thread main loop, queueing policy, and wake conditions beyond thread creation.
Full control table layouts, permissions, and units for virtual memory sysctls.
Complete type definitions, sizes, and alignment for domain, writeback, throttle, node, and zone objects.
Global lock ordering among killer, task, address space, and writeback locks.
Remainder of device limit logic and the polled interval helper beyond the truncated fragment.
Container domain mapping, fraction estimator internals, and timer lifecycle outside shown callers.
Victim selection scoring, adjustment semantics, and signal lifetime beyond observed binding.
Bandwidth averaging update rule and freerun ceiling computation not shown in these fragments.

findings.text: Boot initialization launches a dedicated out of memory reaper thread and, when control interface support is compiled in, registers the virtual memory control table. The initializer is attached to the subsystem boot hook so it runs once during startup.
A public exit helper clears the per task memory death indicator and decrements the global victim counter, waking all waiters on the victim queue when the count reaches zero.

Two public controls manage a global disabled flag for the killer. Enabling clears the flag. Disabling sets it and then waits for in flight victims to drain, restoring the enabled state if the wait times out or is interrupted.

Victim marking expects the global killer lock held, the killer enabled, and a stable non null address space for the target. It runs only once per task via atomic test and set on the death indicator, binds the address space once to the signal lifetime with reference counting, thaws the task so freezer sleep cannot livelock reclaim, increments the victim count, and emits a trace tied to the task credential.
Public add and remove helpers manage caller blocks on the global out of memory notification chain and return the underlying chain operation result.

A container membership iterator skips the most protected adjustment value and the global init task; for other tasks it takes a task reference and invokes the core kill routine with the caller message, always returning success so iteration continues.

A fault path entry synchronizes first with container out of memory state and returns early when that path handled the event or when the current task already has a fatal signal pending. Otherwise it emits a rate limited diagnostic about a leaked fault error, implying the caller retries.

A system call takes a process file descriptor and flags. It rejects any nonzero flags, resolves the descriptor to a task, locates a thread holding the address space, and permits reclamation only when the target will free memory or was previously marked to skip. It then revalidates the skip mark under lock and attempts to reap the address space.

Disabling acquires the global killer mutex in killable mode and releases it after setting the disabled flag. It then sleeps interruptibly with timeout on the victim wait queue until the atomic victim count reads zero.

The release path holds a task reference, stabilizes the address space through the lock task helper, takes an address space reference, then acquires the readable address space lock in killable mode for revalidation and reaping. References and locks are released in reverse order on all exits.

Bandwidth restart samples time and the writeback inode count without locking, and only when idle beyond one interval with no active inodes does it take the device list spinlock to snapshot dirtied and written statistics with the timestamp.

Enabled flag plus victim count form a quiesce machine. Idle is enabled with zero victims. Marking increments victims. Exit decrements and wakes when reaching zero. Disable moves to disabled and waits for zero; timeout or interrupt moves back to enabled.

Completion accounting uses a stopped versus armed timer. Zero timestamp means stopped. First writeout after stop arms the timer one period ahead. Timer expiry advances fractional aging by missed periods plus one and re arms, or clears the timestamp to stop when aging has zeroed all fractions.

Pause ceiling is the larger of one tick and one fifth of the tick rate. Bandwidth sampling uses the same fifth tick floor with minimum one. Completion period spans three ticks. Bandwidth idle detection uses a single tick.
Rate math uses ten bits of fixed point shift. Poll batch threshold starts from one hundred twenty eight entries scaled down as page size grows above one kilobyte.

Initial policy uses thirty two rate pages, ten percent background and twenty percent throttle ratios with byte overrides cleared, high memory dirtyable disabled, writeback wake every five hundred centiseconds, expiry after three thousand centiseconds, one global domain object, and zeroed device minimum ratio.

With container writeback support the throttle initializer binds the global domain, validity reflects domain presence, and completion lookup returns per device container counters. Without that support the initializer is empty, validity is always false, and lookup returns null.
Node dirtyable capacity sums free pages across populated zones only, subtracts the node reserve capped at that free total so kernel reserves are excluded, then adds inactive and active file pages.

Node dirty limit converts the global throttle setting into a node proportional share from byte or percent form, adds one quarter headroom for real time and deadline tasks, and clamps to thirty two bit maximum to bound the dirty ceiling.
Node health is true when the sum of file dirty plus writeback pages on the node does not exceed the node limit.

Four control handlers keep percent and byte forms mutually exclusive and validate range. Writing a ratio clears the paired byte value; writing bytes clears the paired ratio after checking the page rounded value fits thirty two bits, restoring the old value on overflow. Throttle limit changes also refresh the global rate limit.

Device writeout adds the written count to the device statistic and records the same amount in the global domain with the device share fraction, plus the container domain when one exists for the device.
The position curve maps setpoint, current dirty, and limit into a scaled ratio using a cubic shape in normalized distance with unit offset, clamped between zero and twice full scale.

Throttle position defaults to zero and stays zero at or above the hard limit. Otherwise the global target is midway between freerun ceiling and limit and yields a base curve value. Strict limit devices also compute a device local curve from device dirty against device threshold and keep the smaller of the two. Other devices scale the global target by device share, apply a bandwidth dependent linear correction with quarter fallback, then boost when device dirty is below half its threshold.

Poll interval is one when over threshold and otherwise grows with headroom. Maximum pause divides device dirty by a bandwidth scaled rate and caps at the global ceiling. Minimum pause targets about ten milliseconds adjusted for concurrency between bandwidth and rate orders, derives batch size from rate and interval favoring the poll threshold floor, then trims batch so implied pause respects the maximum.
Device thresholds derive device share from the global threshold and scale background proportionally, forcing zero device background when the global threshold is zero.

The release call reports invalid argument for nonzero flags or non reapable targets without skip, missing target when no address space remains, interrupted when the readable lock is killed, try again when reaping made no progress without skip, and not implemented without memory management support.
The writeback domain as observed carries at least a completions estimator, a period timestamp where zero means stopped, and a period timer.

The per device writeback object as observed carries at least global and container completion counters, average write bandwidth and dirty rate limit, bandwidth timestamp with dirtied and written stamps, backing device share and capability flags, a list lock with writeback inode count, and dirtied versus written statistics.

The throttle control object as observed carries at least a domain pointer, a device writeback pointer, global dirty with threshold and background threshold plus hard limit, device dirty with device thresholds, and a computed position ratio.
Marking races container handling and freezer sleep. Single execution guards prevent double flagging and double binding, and thawing prevents a frozen victim from blocking reclaim forever.

Disable can fail when lock acquisition is killed or victims fail to drain in time; on failure it re enables so the system does not remain without killer protection, and it checks that the caller was not itself killed via shared memory.

Byte thresholds are page rounded and range checked against thirty two bit maximum with old value restore; divisors in ratio math are guarded against zero; wide intermediates are clamped; node limits are clamped to preserve the thirty two bit assumption.

Concurrent first writeouts may race to arm the period timer with only approximate expiry as effect; timer re arm uses missed period count so delayed firing still ages correctly; bandwidth restart tolerates stale unlocked samples because the locked snapshot is the commit point.

The release path checks the skip mark before locking and again under lock to observe concurrent exit changes; it treats already reaped work as success and only reports invalid argument when no work was done and no skip was requested.
